title: Relative coherent limit and colimit diagrams
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets and right-pinched mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a simplicial set $K$, let $K^{\triangleright}=K\star\Delta^0$ and $K^{\triangleleft}=\Delta^0\star K$ be the join cones: a simplex is a simplex of either factor or an ordered concatenation of simplices of the two factors. Fix a functor $p:\mathcal D\to\mathcal B$ of quasicategories. For a diagram $q:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal D$, call $q$ a $p$-colimit diagram when, for every diagram $t:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal D$, the square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal D)}(q,t)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)}(q|_K,t|_K)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal B)}(pq,pt)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)}(pq|_K,pt|_K)
\end{array}$$
is a homotopy pullback, the horizontal maps being restriction and the vertical maps postcomposition by $p$. A square of spaces is a homotopy pullback when its comparison to the path model of the pullback is an equivalence; that model consists of a pair of points and a path between their images, retaining all higher simplices. For $q:K^{\triangleleft}\to\mathcal D$, the term $p$-limit diagram is defined by the same square with $(t,q)$ in place of $(q,t)$ and $K^{\triangleleft}$ in place of $K^{\triangleright}$. No existence of such diagrams is part of this definition.
